notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l002: Карган is the best visual reading; it appears to mean aged people here, though the form may be nonstandard or abbreviated.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l004: мүлктүн is a contextual reading of tightly joined handwriting; the final word clearly reads баарысын.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l005: The opening word appears to be Зарын, but the phrase is idiomatically uncertain.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l006: айрыны жамбашты is the closest letter-shape reading; the livestock or feast expression and English remain unresolved.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l010: The first phrase looks like Таң тамаша; it may represent the conventional expression таң-тамаша.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l011: The final verb appears to be баткызат; tense and exact idiomatic force are provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l014: сан is visually likely and is rendered as many; the compact phrase may carry a specialized feast sense.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l015: The manuscript reads Бул үчүн; the referent and the precise sense of арттырып are context-dependent.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l018: кыл жойтуп is the best visual reading, but the described custom and therefore the English are uncertain.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l019: Кыштырата is a tentative reading of the underlined first word; жордуруп is clearer.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l021: Чубайууга is the visible form; its specialized racing sense is uncertain.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l024: The age-class words are legible, but the syntax is compressed; бышты and кунан denote horse age classes.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l025: жазасын literally suggests punishment or fate; in this racing context the English is provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l027: Угаган is an unresolved letter-shape reading; тийген ургаачы is clearer. The English follows the prize context.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l028: The age-class terms are visible, but their grammatical relation to the surrounding lines is uncertain.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l029: The baseline is fully visible but the middle word looks like козуго and is lexically unresolved; the English is contextual.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l030: Both оролорду and чор кокту are tentative letter-shape readings of a difficult line; the English only conveys the apparent collective action.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf017:l031: The words are visually clear, but жазасын is rendered as award from the racing context rather than its usual sense punishment; the sentence continues on the next page.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l001: The first word appears to be the proper name Зайтакер; the syntax and reading of соңку are provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l002: The overwritten opening word is best read Таасын; its first medial letters remain obscured.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l003: Кара кылса is the best visual reading, but the idiom and translation are provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l004: The final name looks like Кызырын, but its ending is compressed and may be inflectional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l005: Бышты and байгесин are visually likely; the elliptical relation between them remains provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l007: The last word is faint and provisionally read жортуна; translation follows that reading.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l011: Өзөк is visually plausible, though the first word's medial letters are lightly written.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l012: The line is legible as written, but андай may instead be a similarly shaped demonstrative and the English is contextual.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l013: мындан is the best reading of the faint central word; the phrase is elliptical.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l015: The opening word is overwritten but context and visible letter shapes support Баатыр.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l017: салган is the likeliest reading of the joined central word; translation is contextual.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l018: The final noun appears to be чокусу; the comparative construction is provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l019: The opening word and the proper-name reading Кара Көз are tentative; the manuscript joins are faint.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l020: The second ethnonym is provisionally normalized as Таргоот from faint handwriting.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l024: The line visually reads миң кара, but the livestock noun is elliptical and the English supplies the contextual referent.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l026: The ending балдардан is visually likely, but the case relation and English remain provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l027: Арын уйкаш is a best-effort reading of pale, joined handwriting; translation conveys only the apparent ordering sense.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l029: Сай кара is visually clear but elliptical; livestock is supplied contextually in English.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l032: ойкулдан is a tentative reading of the faint central word; translation is contextual.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l033: The final word looks like туулган, though the feast context may imply a different verb; English is contextual.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf018:l034: The short final line is pale; дуу болуп is the best contextual reading and continues syntactically onto the next page.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l001: Калатайын is the best visual reading; the proper name or lexeme is not securely identified, so the English transliterates it.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l002: The joined middle and final letters are faint; Козакбайын is a provisional proper-name reading.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l003: The first word appears to be бүлөөн, an uncertain dialectal or manuscript form; translation is contextual.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l005: Элигип and бук are visually plausible but the idiom is unresolved; English is provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l015: The final word appears as чериге; syntax and translation are provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l016: Чымайымдын is a provisional proper-name reading.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l017: The grammatical form өзүңдү is visually plausible but may represent another possessive form.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l018: A word is struck through before the retained name Хан Теңир; Бөрүнүн каны is the best reading of the uncrossed text.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l020: Урайынан is the best visual reading; it is interpreted as lineage here.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l021: Both words are tightly joined and pale; reading and figurative translation are provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l022: This is a low-confidence reading of a faint baseline; English gives only the apparent genealogical sense.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l023: Чуңка and тоорасы are best-effort readings; heir is a contextual rendering of the unresolved final noun.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l024: Калкандын could alternatively be калкымдын; the place or collective reference is unresolved.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l026: The final word is especially faint and is transcribed provisionally as кырчылгы.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l027: сайынган is visually likely; the martial English sense is contextual.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l028: The line is pale; Базарга кийген is the closest reading, but the formula may be different.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l029: The first two words are faint and compressed; translation follows the clearer заары көп.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l033: Таңкулуу башка is a low-confidence reading of pale connected script; English is provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l034: так is read as throne; the manuscript spacing permits айбаттак as a single unclear form.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l035: The third word is clearly кыргыз; тулган is a provisional reading of the following pale word.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf019:l036: The final baseline is pale, ends incompletely, and continues onto the next manuscript page; чыгабы is the best reading.
